reason: The lane-born stars are approaching the returning galaxy, so its stellar outskirts are the natural place to follow them.

choice.combine: Young stars from the dark lane
choice.with: Stellar outskirts of the returning galaxy

expectation: The stars will pass through the outskirts, with their paths altered by the encounter.

effect: The stars crossed the returning galaxy with altered paths, completing the goal and showing how differently stars and their parent gas clouds encounter one another.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the contrast with the earlier gas collision.

mostWorthwhile.text: Sending the lane-born stars through the stellar outskirts was worthwhile because it made the contrast between stellar and gas-cloud encounters clear.

leastWorthwhile.text: There was no particularly confusing or repetitive passage in this short chapter.

surprise.text: The crossing emphasized that matter once spread through colliding clouds is now concentrated in widely separated stars that pass among other stars.

arbitrary.text: The combination had a clear purpose: the stars were approaching the returning galaxy, and its outskirts were the relevant location.

continue.text: I would continue: the crossing tied the stars' origins to the evolving shared galaxy, and I would be curious to see what happens next.
